findings.claim: The duplicate-key guard is applied unevenly. In the second member loop (the field loop, around new line 1160), `intMembers.Add(member.IntKey, ...)` is still unguarded, while the string-key Add in the same loop (line 1176) and both Adds in the property loop now are guarded. Two concrete inputs reach the unguarded Add: two `[Key(0)]` fields, or a `[Key(0)]` property plus a `[Key(0)]` field. Either throws ArgumentException ('An item with the same key has already been added') inside TypeCollector. The analyzer then dies with AD0001, so no MsgPack0xx diagnostics are reported for that type, and the generator dies with CS8785. This holds with or without `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, so for integer-keyed field members the crash class this change hardens against is still present.

findings.claim: `if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(...))` and `if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(...))` keep the first member and silently drop any later member with the same key, without reporting a diagnostic at that point. Example input: two distinct non-overridden properties `[Key(0)] public int A` and `[Key(0)] public int B`, with source generation not suppressed. A formatter is generated that never serializes B. On base this input crashed loudly; on head it silently loses data. DynamicObjectResolver rejects duplicate keys at run time, so the generated formatter and the dynamic formatter also disagree.
